claims.text: Adding an intermediate-temperature dwell during rapid heating activates atomic diffusivity.
Dwell-activated diffusivity promotes redistributive atomic mixing.
The intermediate-temperature dwell promotes homogeneous nucleation.
Improved mixing and homogeneous nucleation direct formation of uniform, single-phase, solid-solution noble-metal HEA nanoparticles.
The proposed starting material is a fixed-composition precursor mixture containing noble metals such as Pt, Pd, Au, Ag, Rh, and Ir.
The controlled intervention consists of a 300–400 °C dwell for 5–15 minutes before rapid heating to the final synthesis temperature.
An inert atmosphere prevents oxidation or other unwanted side reactions during processing.
Atomic diffusivity during the dwell improves atomic mixing.
Atomic diffusivity during the dwell enables controlled pre-nucleation ordering.
The dwell gives atoms sufficient mobility for local redistributive mixing.
The dwell initiates homogeneous nucleation.
Redistributive mixing and homogeneous nucleation reduce local composition fluctuations.
Reducing local composition fluctuations suppresses phase separation and elemental segregation.
The dwell reduces uncontrolled nanoparticle morphology relative to continuous rapid heating and cooling.
Dwell-treated nanoparticles will have greater single-phase uniformity, less elemental segregation, and more controlled morphology than the no-dwell baseline.
The resulting solid solution is likely to be FCC when FCC is thermodynamically favored.
Continuous rapid heating and cooling without a dwell often produces phase separation, elemental segregation, or non-equilibrium nucleation.
Temperatures below approximately 300 °C may provide insufficient atomic diffusivity.
Temperatures above approximately 400 °C or dwell times longer than 15 minutes may cause premature nucleation.
Temperatures above approximately 400 °C or dwell times longer than 15 minutes may cause particle coarsening.
